summary: Legally low-risk: defensive content, holds no customer logs, minimal dual-use. Fixable issues: liability when a pack drops events a client's regulator, contract or incident needed; employee-monitoring law for per-user access reports; data custody in the tuning and log-diet steps; attribution duties for CC-BY/DRL-licensed upstream content; no redistributing standalone Sysmon.

objections.objection: Volume reduction can push an MSSP's client below its own logging or retention duties (PCI DSS Req. 10, HIPAA 164.312(b) audit controls, NIS2 or cyber-insurance terms). When an incident needs a dropped event, the MSSP will point to QuietWin's 'detections still covered' claim. The concept names the liability risk but leaves contract language as an open question, and a solo founder has no tech E&O cover budgeted.
objections.evidence: concept:risks[3]; concept:open_questions[3]; concept:mvp.features[4] (coverage-versus-volume report claims detections still covered)

objections.objection: The logon evidence pack produces per-client monthly reports of who logged in, session length and privilege use, which is employee monitoring. In the EU this needs a legal basis, transparency and proportionality under GDPR, and often a DPIA. In Germany it is subject to works-council co-determination for technical monitoring devices (BetrVG s.87(1) no.6). The MSP's client is the controller, but packs and report templates shipped without guidance expose the MSP and invite misuse.
objections.evidence: concept:mvp.features[2]; concept:user (MSP technicians hand the monthly per-client access report to the client)

objections.objection: Data custody is not quite 'no customer logs'. The 5-day tuning engagement and the log-diet script run against client collectors holding usernames, IPs and command lines. The founder needs a DPA/sub-processor position, NDAs and a script that provably keeps data local, or MSSPs bound by their own client contracts can't let them in.
objections.evidence: concept:mvp.features[6]; concept:go_to_market.wedge (run one script on a client's collector)

objections.objection: Upstream content carries licence duties. SwiftOnSecurity sysmon-config is CC BY 4.0 (attribution in the text). SigmaHQ rules are DRL 1.1, which requires crediting the rule author in any view that shows matches, so the per-SIEM output mappings must carry author fields. sysmon-modular is MIT. A paid pack that quietly forks these without attribution is both an ethics problem and a reputational risk in this community.

Standalone Sysmon is still needed for pre-2025 Server and Windows 10 fleets, and the Sysinternals licence forbids publishing the software for others to copy. RMM scripts must fetch it from Microsoft rather than bundle the binary.

Mild dual-use: a public, ATT&CK-mapped list of which events the standard pack drops tells attackers what MSSP clients are blind to. Keep drop rationale for less-common events in the paid tier, or document compensating detections.

strongest_point: Ships configuration content, not a hosted service. It holds no customer logs and runs no privileged agent, and dropping unneeded events serves data minimisation, so the regulatory and abuse surface is small.
what_would_change_my_mind: A lawyer-reviewed subscription agreement with a liability cap, a no-warranty-of-completeness clause and a client-acknowledgement step before any pack drops events
A per-pack table mapping kept events to PCI DSS 10, HIPAA 164.312(b) and NIS2 logging duties
An EU-ready employee-monitoring notice and DPIA template shipped with the logon evidence report
A data-handling statement for the tuning engagement and log-diet script (local-only processing, DPA template)
Tech E&O insurance quoted at under $2k/year
